[i]Irman looked the man up and down before nodding and bowing in kind. "Correct." He walked off toward the great marble door of the palace, carved upon it was the Shahada which itself was emblazoned with foreign gold. As he walked the halls, stepping upon a fine Iroccan carpet, passing by the artworks of the long past golden age a faint smile grew upon his face. Guards littered the Palace, each of them well equipped to ensure the safety of the Sealiph who had done so much good in the name of the state and Allah. Soon enough they reached a grand hall decorated with calligraphy and artworks much like the hallway they had just walked through.

In a corner there was a grand library, each book's cover seemed ancient and well worn. And there was the throne, it was simple, more of a chair than a grand throne. It was covered in pillows, more for the comfort of the aging man who sat upon it than the prestige which thrones are normally used for. Upon it sat the Sealiph, his face well worn and wrinkled, his grey beard stretching to his chest and his bushy eyebrows furrowed as they entered. He looked so small upon that seat, though that did not change his regality. A fine turban upon his head and a silk robe draped over his body, with a great cape that was edged in fur finishing off his look.

He extended his hand out toward the visitors. "Unto my home came a visitor from alien lands, with dignity I granted him access and spoke to him like a brother lost to time." A seat was swiftly fetched for Chul if he wished to take it. Irman placed himself next to the door. Ever watching ever vigilant.[/i]
